name: Pashur (priest who struck Jeremiah)
title: The temple overseer who persecuted the prophet
summary: Pashur was the son of Immer and a temple overseer in Jerusalem. He is known for striking the prophet Jeremiah and putting him in stocks at the Benjamin Gate because he prophesied about the fall of Jerusalem. Jeremiah gave him a new name, Magor-Missabib, which means 'terror on every side'.

keyEvents.title: Striking Jeremiah and putting him in stocks
keyEvents.description: Pashur heard Jeremiah's prophecies about the destruction of Jerusalem and responded by striking the prophet and placing him in stocks at the upper Benjamin Gate in the temple.

keyEvents.title: Releasing Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: The next day, Pashur released Jeremiah from the stocks, but the prophet continued to proclaim God's judgment.

keyEvents.title: Receiving the name Magor-Missabib
keyEvents.description: Jeremiah gave Pashur a new name, Magor-Missabib ('terror on every side'), as a prophecy that he and all his friends would become a terror to themselves.

keyEvents.title: Prophecy of exile and death
keyEvents.description: Jeremiah prophesied that Pashur and his entire household would be taken to Babylon, and that he would die there and be buried with all his friends for whom he had prophesied lies.
